items.title: 67246_Buck Clayton oral history interview
items.q: Me and, there were three trumpets and my father was on the bass at that time.

ctx.x: He did when I, when, as he got older. He gradually got away from that cornet and when I was learning trumpet, which he taught me, the scales, but I already knew how to read from playing piano. And we had a chapel orchestra that played for churches, funerals and social affairs in the park on Sunday afternoons and we rehearsed at my house, every Sunday. And my dad played tuba then.

Me and, there were three trumpets and my father was on the bass at that time. You see, but earlier during the years like when King Oliver was in New Orleans, my dad was in Texas playing trumpet, cornet, rather.
Well was he sort of playing in the equivalent of jazz orchestras at that time?
